levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: No assumption is named.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets

levels.label: Not yet

levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known and how it limits the conclusion.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The criteria are not used.

levels.label: Meets

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: Recommend one of the three fictional roles for someone who needs steady income within six months, and defend it against the role with the highest total compensation.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Recommends a role and grounds it in the six-month constraint, not only in total compensation.
Faces the strongest counter-argument directly: Role 3 pays $20,484 a year more than Role 1 but cannot deliver any income for 24 months.
Uses the recoup figures — 8 months for Role 2, 35 months from enrolment for Role 3 — rather than comparing program costs alone.
evidenceRequirements: Cites at least one total-compensation figure and at least one recoup figure computed in this lesson.
lookFors: The response treats the six-month constraint as binding rather than mentioning it and then choosing on pay.
A recommendation of Role 2 must acknowledge that its 9-month program also breaks the six-month constraint; only Role 1 satisfies it outright.
judgment.commonMisconception: Ranking career paths by their eventual pay while ignoring how long the person has to survive on nothing.

judgment.prompt: State one figure in your three income profiles that you are least confident in, and say what would change your recommendation if it were wrong.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Names a specific figure from the profiles rather than expressing general uncertainty.
Says concretely how the recommendation would change if that figure were different, including the direction and rough size of change that would matter.
evidenceRequirements: Refers to a specific computed figure from this lesson by value.
lookFors: The response identifies an assumption that is actually load-bearing, such as the 2,080-hour full-time year or the benefit valuations.
The response does not simply say all the numbers are made up.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
oracle.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic over BigInt; no binary floating point
oracle.limits: Recomputation establishes that the key follows from the stated figures. It does not by itself establish that the model chosen is the right model for the scenario; that is carried by the per-item reasoning, the parameter-visibility check, and human review.
